title: On the Quartic-free A-groups
summary: A finite group is said to be quartic-free if its order is not divisible by $p^4$ of any prime $p$. A finite group is called an $A$-group if all of its Sylow subgroups are abelian. Objective of this paper is to provide explicit structure of a quartic-free $A$-group. Further in the process of providing the explicit structure we also determine the derived length of a solvable quartic-free $A$-group.
